items.prompt: Which word has two meanings: a flying animal and a piece of sports equipment?

options.why: A ball is used in sport, but it is not an animal.
A net is sports equipment, but it is not an animal.
An owl flies, but it is not sports equipment.

hints: A word with two meanings and one spelling is a homonym.
Think of an animal that flies at night.
Then think of something used to hit a ball. Do they share a name?
items.explanation: Bat is a homonym. It can mean a flying animal or the piece of equipment used in sports such as cricket.

options.why: After a vowel, the shul ending is usually spelt -cial.
This spells the sound, but not the correct letters.
The i and the a are in the wrong order.

hints: Say the word slowly: spe-shul.
After a vowel, the shul ending is usually spelt -cial, as in official.
Write spe, then add the ending.
items.explanation: Special ends in -cial, like official and social. The -cial ending usually follows a vowel.

items.prompt: Match each sentence to the meaning of the word in it.
pairs: Wind the string around the stick.
A tear rolled down her cheek.
a drop of water from the eye
to save sound to play later
hints: Each pair of sentences uses the same spelling with a different meaning.
Say each sentence aloud. The word may sound different too.
Start with the wind. Is it moving air or turning something?
items.explanation: Wind, tear and record are homographs: they are spelt the same but have different meanings, and they are often pronounced differently.

items.prompt: In which sentence does bank mean the side of a river?

options.text: Mum put the money in the bank.
options.why: Here bank means a place that keeps money.

options.text: We had a picnic on the bank of the Brantas River.
You can bank on me to help.
options.why: Here bank on means rely on.

options.text: The plane began to bank to the left.
options.why: Here bank means tilt to one side while turning.

hints: Bank is a homonym with several meanings.
Look for clue words near bank in each sentence.
Read the words that come straight after bank.
items.explanation: In the picnic sentence, the clue river shows that bank means the land along the side of the water.

items.prompt: Write the full words using -cial or -tial. The par___ eclipse lasted an hour. Here is the offi___ timetable.
hints: Listen for the letter just before the shul sound.
-tial usually follows a consonant, and -cial usually follows a vowel.
Look at the last letter before the gap in each word.
items.explanation: Partial has r before the ending, so it takes -tial. Official has i before the ending, so it takes -cial.

options.why: Confident ends in -ent, so the noun ends in -ence.
The ending is spelt -ence, with a c.
The second vowel is i: con-fi-dence.

hints: Think of the adjective: confident.
If an adjective ends in -ent, the noun usually ends in -ence.
Write confident, then change the last letters.
items.explanation: Confident becomes confidence. Adjectives ending in -ent usually make nouns ending in -ence, like patient and patience.

options.why: Words ending in -ible change to -ibly.
The root is horrible, so the ending is -ibly.
The -le changes to -ly. You do not keep the e.

hints: The root word is horrible.
Words ending in -le change the -le to -ly.
Write horrible, then change its last two letters.
items.explanation: Horrible ends in -le, so the -le changes to -ly: horribly, like sensibly and gently.

items.prompt: Add -ed to each verb. prefer: ___ visit: ___
hints: Say each verb and listen for which syllable is stressed.
If the last syllable is stressed and ends in one vowel and one consonant, double the consonant.
Say pre-FER and VIS-it. Which one is stressed at the end?
items.explanation: Prefer is stressed at the end, so the r doubles: preferred. Visit is stressed at the start, so the t does not double: visited.

items.prompt: Choose all the words that are spelt correctly.

options.why: Occur is stressed at the end, so the r doubles: occurred.
Refer is stressed at the end, so the r doubles: referred.
Garden is stressed at the start, so the n does not double: gardening.

hints: Look carefully at the double letters.
When a word is stressed on its last syllable, the final consonant usually doubles before -ed or -ing.
Say each root word and clap the syllables. Where is the stress?
items.explanation: Travelled (the British spelling), beginning and forgotten are correct. The others should be occurred, referred and gardening.

items.prompt: Which word fits all three gaps? We can ___ the car here. The ___ has a big pond. Let’s play in the ___ after school.

options.why: Leave fits the first gap only.
Garden fits the last two gaps, but you cannot garden a car.
Stop fits the first gap only.

hints: The word is a homonym with more than one meaning.
Test each option in all three gaps.
Start with the first gap: what can you do with a car?
items.explanation: Park is a homonym. It means to leave a car somewhere, and it also means a public garden with a pond or a playground.
